reason: The well needs an extraction head to bring water up from the surveyed ice.
expectation: I expect the head to be installed at the bore, though it may need further connections before water flows.

alternatives.reason: Foil and felt might make insulation, but establishing extraction seems more direct.

effect: The sealed well now produces cloudy meltwater, so it needs a route to treatment.
reaction: The closed, heated well is a satisfying practical start.
reason: A clean hose should connect the well to the treatment line.
expectation: I expect the hose to attach to the well, possibly requiring another step to reach the processor.

alternatives.reason: Insulation may be useful later, but the water connection is more immediate.

effect: The heated hose connects the well to the processor, with a strainer catching grit before treatment.
reaction: The upstream strainer is a useful, concrete detail.
reason: The connected line is ready to use at the water processor, directly advancing treatment.
expectation: I expect the processor to treat the raw water, though additional setup may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Foil and felt may make insulation, but treatment is the immediate goal.

effect: The treated water is in the buffer tank, and the remaining goal is to protect the exterior run.
reaction: The first cup is a quiet, satisfying payoff.
reason: The only offered combination appears to make insulation for the exterior run.
expectation: I expect the foil and felt to form a protective insulating wrap, though fitting it may take another step.

effect: The foil and felt made reflective insulation, ready to fit to the well line.
reaction: The result was predictable, with no additional detail.
reason: The only offered combination should protect the exterior water line.
expectation: I expect the insulation to wrap the connected well line and help protect it from heat loss.

effect: The insulated, heat-traced line completes the chapter and clarifies that insulation slows heat loss rather than supplying heat.
reaction: The distinction between insulation and active heating was a satisfying practical detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting insulation to the heated hose was most worthwhile: it completed the system and explained why the hose still needs heat tracing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the reflective insulation was predictable and gave no detail until it was fitted.

surprise.text: The hose was already heated when connected, and its strainer caught grit upstream of treatment; that made the line more substantial than a simple pipe.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining foil and felt was an obvious, menu-led step rather than a discovery.

continue.text: Yes. The practical details made building the water system satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the expedition develops, though the choices were fairly straightforward.
